newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil high court due to rule on CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil high court due to rule on CVRD sale.

text.p: Brazil's highest court was due to rule Wednesday on one of two lawsuits brought by a lawyers' group alleging that government plans to privatize state miner Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) are unconstitutional.
A full meeting of the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) was due to begin at 1400 local/1700 GMT, an STF spokesman said.
The Order of Brazilian Lawyers (OAB) last week filed two Actions of Unconstitutionality against the government seeking injunctions to halt the privatization.
The government aims to sell a 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD at an auction on April 29.
Meanwhile, an STF judge who on Tuesday granted an injunction against the government was studying the possibility of reconsidering his decision after a government appeal, the STF spokesman said.
The injuction bars the federal transfer of 412,000 hectares near the Carajas mine to CVRD.
Justice Marco Aurelio de Mello would probably announce later Wednesday whether or not he would reconsider his injunction.
If Mello declines to reconsider the case, the appeal would move automatically for a full hearing. No date for the full meeting has been set.
